verdict.rationale: Rootly documents an official MCP server that exposes incident data and actions to MCP clients such as Claude Code and Cursor, and the docs say agents can "take action." It also documents an API for creating incidents automatically, with API keys scoped to On-Call and Incident Response roles. However, the evidence never shows that acknowledging, escalating, and resolving are actually exposed through the API or MCP tools, so end-to-end lifecycle control without a dashboard is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit acknowledge/escalate/resolve endpoints or MCP tools, a machine-readable API spec (OpenAPI probes returned 404), and hands-on corroboration of agent-driven end-to-end handling.
